title: College, Consent, Money & Mind

myths.myth: If they didn't say no, it's a yes.
myths.truth: Consent is an active, enthusiastic yes — not the absence of a no.
myths.explanation: Silence, freezing or going along with it isn't consent.

myths.myth: We're together, so consent is assumed.
myths.truth: Every time is a fresh yes — a relationship isn't blanket consent.
myths.explanation: Being a couple never removes the need to check in.

myths.myth: They were drunk, but it still counts.
myths.truth: Someone too drunk to agree can't consent.
myths.explanation: Alcohol or incapacitation removes the capacity to consent.

myths.myth: What they wore — or coming over — means they wanted it.
myths.truth: Clothes, flirting or coming over are never consent.
myths.explanation: Nothing about a person implies a yes; only a yes does.

myths.myth: If they seem nice online, they are who they say.
myths.truth: Catfishing is common — verify before you trust or meet.
myths.explanation: Video-call and check details before meeting a match.

myths.myth: Meeting a match alone is fine if you click.
myths.truth: Meet in public, tell a friend, keep an exit plan.
myths.explanation: Good first-date safety habits aren't paranoid — they're normal.

myths.myth: Ghosting is just easier for everyone.
myths.truth: A kind, honest 'no thanks' beats leaving someone hanging.
myths.explanation: Respect goes both ways, even when you're not interested.

myths.myth: A rejection means something's wrong with me.
myths.truth: Not matching is about fit, not your worth.
myths.explanation: Handling rejection — and giving it kindly — is a dating skill.

myths.myth: Jealousy means they really love me.
myths.truth: Controlling jealousy is a red flag, not love.
myths.explanation: Healthy love is built on trust, not surveillance.

myths.myth: They check my phone because they care.
myths.truth: Monitoring and isolation are control, not protection.
myths.explanation: Coercive control often hides behind 'I'm just protective'.

myths.myth: Healthy couples never fight.
myths.truth: Conflict is normal — repairing afterwards is what matters.
myths.explanation: How you handle and mend a fight beats never having one.

myths.myth: Love means losing yourself in someone.
myths.truth: Healthy love keeps room for your own friends and life.
myths.explanation: Independence inside a relationship is a sign of health.

myths.myth: Getting tested means you've done something wrong.
myths.truth: Routine STI testing is normal self-care.
myths.explanation: Testing is part of looking after your body, not a verdict.

myths.myth: Contraception is the woman's job.
myths.truth: Contraception and sexual health are a shared responsibility.
myths.explanation: Both partners own the choices and the conversation.

myths.myth: Pleasure isn't something to talk about.
myths.truth: Wellbeing and pleasure, within consent, are a healthy part of life.
myths.explanation: Honest communication makes intimacy safer and better.

myths.myth: Clinics will judge me or tell my family.
myths.truth: Adult sexual-health services are confidential.
myths.explanation: You have a right to private, non-judgmental care.

myths.myth: He handles the money — that's just how it works.
myths.truth: Both partners deserve a say and their own financial footing.
myths.explanation: Shared, transparent money is a sign of an equal partnership.

myths.myth: Budgeting is only for people short on money.
myths.truth: A budget is how anyone stays in control of their money.
myths.explanation: Knowing where it goes is the first step to independence.

myths.myth: Controlling all the money is a way of caring.
myths.truth: Cutting off access to money is financial abuse.
myths.explanation: Everyone in a relationship needs their own access to money.

myths.myth: Asking about pay is rude.
myths.truth: Knowing your worth and negotiating pay is your right.
myths.explanation: Talking about money is how you avoid being short-changed.

myths.myth: Asking for help means I'm failing.
myths.truth: Reaching out is a strength — and it works.
myths.explanation: Getting support early is the smart move, not a weakness.

myths.myth: Everyone else has settled in fine.
myths.truth: Loneliness at college is common — and it passes.
myths.explanation: Most people feel adrift at first; belonging is built slowly.

myths.myth: Homesickness is childish.
myths.truth: Missing home is a normal part of a big move.
myths.explanation: Leaving home is one of life's hardest transitions.

myths.myth: My worth depends on how I look.
myths.truth: Your worth isn't your body or your feed.
myths.explanation: Protecting body image and self-worth is part of staying well.

myths.myth: Everyone else has it all figured out.
myths.truth: No one does — they're just better at hiding the mess.
myths.explanation: The comparison spiral is a feeling, not the facts.

myths.myth: My worth is my CV and my package.
myths.truth: Your worth isn't a salary or a job title.
myths.explanation: Who you are is bigger than what you do for work.

myths.myth: A setback means I've failed.
myths.truth: Failure is information, not a verdict.
myths.explanation: Setbacks tell you what to try next, not who you are.

myths.myth: If I'm not succeeding by now, I never will.
myths.truth: There's no single timeline — your path is yours.
myths.explanation: Lives unfold at different speeds; comparison lies.

myths.myth: Speaking up will just make me look difficult.
myths.truth: Your voice belongs in the room — use it.
myths.explanation: Claiming your voice is leadership, not trouble-making.

myths.myth: The note-taking and tidying can fall to her.
myths.truth: 'Office housework' shouldn't default to women.
myths.explanation: Unseen support work should be shared, not gendered.

myths.myth: She was just being bossy.
myths.truth: The same behaviour gets called 'leadership' in a man.
myths.explanation: Spotting the double standard is the first step to fairness.

myths.myth: It's not my problem if I'm not the target.
myths.truth: Allyship means stepping in, not staying silent.
myths.explanation: Active allyship turns bystanders into upstanders.

myths.myth: If it happens at work, there's nothing I can do.
myths.truth: POSH law gives you an Internal Committee and the right to complain.
myths.explanation: Workplaces and colleges must have a path for harassment complaints.

myths.myth: A landlord can throw me out whenever.
myths.truth: Tenancy rights protect you from arbitrary eviction.
myths.explanation: Renters have legal protections worth knowing.

myths.myth: Online harassment isn't a real crime.
myths.truth: Cyber harassment is illegal and reportable.
myths.explanation: Stalking, threats and image abuse online are offences.

myths.myth: Knowing your rights is only for lawyers.
myths.truth: Your core rights at work and home are yours to use.
myths.explanation: Knowing the redress path is half the protection.
